title: 187 Does selection of beef cattle for production traits impact post-weaning immunological phenotype and robustness traits
content:
Abstract
The objective of this study was to determine the effects of selection focused on performance traits on phenotypic expression of immune competence of growing beef steers. Steers selected for high and moderate growth and high and low milk production traits based on sire expected progeny differences were used in a 2 × 2 factorial arrangement (High growth/High Milk - HH, High growth/Low Milk - HL, Moderate growth/High Milk - MH, and Moderate growth/Low Milk - ML). Steer calves (n = 239) were weaned at the Range Cow Research Center South or North Units for 60 days where animals received a multivalent modified live virus and clostridial bacterin toxoid vaccine before (on d -90) and at weaning (d 0). Calves were administered an intradermal tetanus toxoid bacterin on d 14 to evaluate a Type IV delayed type hypersensitivity reaction (DTH) and magnitude of change in skinfold thickness was measured and calculated 48 h post injection. Steers were assigned to an immune response group 0 to 5, with 0 having no change and 5 having a large change at the reaction site. Additionally, serum collected on d 0, 14, 60, and 88 post weaning was used to analyze clostridial tetanus toxoid antibody levels, bovine viral diarrhea serum neutralizing antibody titers (BVD SNT), and a D2DX immunity test score (D2DX ITS; D2DX, Nano Discovery, Orlando, FL). Following preconditioning, steers were transported 22.5 km to Willard Sparks Beef Research Center for the finishing phase. Data was analyzed using the MIXED procedure of SAS for continuous data and GLIMMIX procedure for categorical data with the contemporary group as the random effect and animal as the experimental unit. Ninety-one percent of steers exhibited a DTH reaction, and 85% of these steers had an average response (± 0.1 mm). All steers BVD SNT increased from d 0 to d 14 by 1.34 (P < 0.01) but plateaued from d 14 to 60 (5.74 vs. 5.71, respectively; P = 0.91). A high D2DX ITS is indicative of a strong type 1 immune response and weak type 2 immune response. At d 60, the day after transport to WSBRC, MH and ML steers tended to have a higher D2DX ITS (0.08; P = 0.10) when exposed to a stressor compared to HH and HM steers but their D2DX ITS returned to similar levels (0.044; P = 0.94) 28 d post transport. During the finishing phase, MH and ML genotypes had more respiratory related mortalities (P = 0.03) than HH and HL steers at an average of 151 days on feed. Moderate growth phenotype steers responded to transport stress by mounting a Type 1 immune response and later had increased BRD related illness and death later in the feeding period.
